jobs.title: Design codex — RFC 0046 V1.7 attestation gap closure
jobs.objective: Design the V1.7 fix for the lane-attestation forgery gap. Required answers (one concrete choice each): (1) Where in src/striatum/daemon_pg/handlers/workflow_loop/submit_review.py::publish_artifact_inline does the new process_executions check go? Cite line range. (2) The exact SQL query that proves a session_id has at least one process_executions row in state IN ('running','completed'). (3) Check-by-session (any process_executions row in the session) vs check-by-artifact (the row's content matches the artifact's SHA256). Justify with threat model: forged byline + operator-shell write must fail; legitimate supervised lane must succeed. (4) New error code + operator hint for the refusal. (5) The RFC 0046 V1 operator-override `--allow-no-process-execution --override-rationale '<reason>'` MUST continue to work (audit-chained). (6) Whether session_lane_attestation in context.py needs to surface process_execution_count for dashboards. (7) Test surface: tests/test_lane_attestation_v17.py — forged byline + no process_executions → refused; supervised path → allowed; override path → allowed with audit; multi-session run.

jobs.title: Review design gemini adversarial threat_model
jobs.objective: Adversarial threat model: (1) Can an operator-shell write + forged byline still publish if they `striatum supervise start` first and never have the supervised process actually run? — the check must require a process_executions row in 'running'/'completed', NOT just an attached process_supervisors row. (2) Can a supervised lane that wrote artifact A trick the runner into accepting artifact B by reusing the process_executions row? — proposed by-artifact check. (3) Does the operator-override path still work? — --allow-no-process-execution MUST land with audit reason. (4) Multi-session coverage test present? Bounce on gaps.
